copy.headline: I'm 17 and I think grocery stores are lying to you.
copy.body: Here's why I'm building an app about it.

copy.headline: I work at a retirement home.
items: Every week I watch perfectly good food get thrown away because no one could see what the kitchen had.
Hundreds of dollars. Every single week.

copy.headline: Then I started reading the research.
items: The average family wastes $2,913/year on food they buy and never eat.
Expiration dates are unregulated suggestions — not safety warnings.
Grocery stores are designed to make you overbuy.

copy.headline: This isn't a personal failure.
copy.body: It's a system designed to extract maximum spending from you while giving you no tools to track what you actually have.

copy.headline: So I taught myself to code.
items: I used Google's AI to build a scanner that reads your grocery receipt and instantly logs every item — with shelf life data, storage instructions, and meal suggestions.

copy.headline: I'm 17. I have no budget, no investors, no team.
copy.body: I built this in my bedroom between homework and AP exams. And I think it can save the average family money.

copy.headline: It's called fond.
copy.ctaLine: Save it before your fridge does the forgetting. Follow for more, something's on the way.
